theme: 3 terms on screen shapes: upright or sideways, the compact or regular label, and a layout that adapts

terms.definition: Whether the screen is shown upright (portrait) or sideways (landscape).
terms.example: Lock the Interface Orientation to portrait for the camera screen.

terms.definition: A simple label, compact or regular, for the width or height available to your app.
terms.example: Check the Size Class before you show the sidebar.

terms.definition: A layout that changes to fit different screen sizes and orientations.
terms.example: We need an Adaptive Layout so the screen works on iPad too.

video.title: Interface Orientation, Size Class & Adaptive Layout | Day 122
video.description:
Learn to explain how an iOS layout adapts to rotation and screen size: Interface Orientation, Size Class & Adaptive Layout, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Interface Orientation - Whether the screen is shown upright (portrait) or sideways (landscape).
Size Class - A simple label, compact or regular, for the width or height available to your app.
Adaptive Layout - A layout that changes to fit different screen sizes and orientations.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: iOS Interface Orientation, Size Class & Adaptive Layout | Day 122
landscape.description:
Explain Interface Orientation, Size Class & Adaptive Layout in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
인터페이스 방향, 사이즈 클래스, 어댑티브 레이아웃 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Interface Orientation - Whether the screen is shown upright (portrait) or sideways (landscape).
한국어: 인터페이스 방향: 화면이 세로(포트레이트)인지 가로(랜드스케이프)인지

Size Class - A simple label, compact or regular, for the width or height available to your app.
한국어: 사이즈 클래스: 앱이 쓸 수 있는 너비나 높이를 compact 또는 regular로 나눈 이름

Adaptive Layout - A layout that changes to fit different screen sizes and orientations.
한국어: 어댑티브 레이아웃: 화면 크기와 방향에 맞춰 바뀌는 레이아웃

In this video, Mina and Jake fix a settings screen that looks tiny on iPad, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Interface Orientation, Size Class and Adaptive Layout in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the settings screen looks tiny on iPad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it an Adaptive Layout, or fixed sizes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use the Size Class. Compact means little space, and regular means more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like in the code, the stack goes vertical when it is compact?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The Size Class is usually compact on iPhone in portrait.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rotation changes the Interface Orientation, and the Size Class may change too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I lock the Interface Orientation to portrait?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, but an Adaptive Layout is better for users.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Agreed. I will test it on iPad.
Lock the Interface Orientation to portrait.
